title: #1 Einstein
prompt: “The only thing that interferes with my learning is education.” – Albert Einstein. What did he mean by that? Do you think he is correct?

variants.label: Version 1: AGREE
variants.essay:
Learning at school can sometimes block real understanding. In my opinion, I strongly agree with the view that school education can sometimes stop real learning. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

School systems sometimes teach things that do not help people learn for life. In other words, the focus is often on passing tests, not on real knowledge in daily life in daily life today. For example, students may learn dates for a test, but they forget the information later. As a result, the learning is only for the test, not for life. This shows that the system teaches facts, but not how to think.

Another reason is that school life can limit a person's own interests. This is because the school must cover many subjects for all students in daily life in daily life. For example, a student who loves art might have to spend time on hard math lessons. As a result, the student feels that their own interests are not important enough. This supports the view that school limits personal passion.

In conclusion, I strongly agree with the view that school education can sometimes stop real learning. This is because the system focuses on passing tests rather than real knowledge, and it can limit a person's own interests by covering many subjects.

analysis.point1: School systems focus on facts, and the school limits personal passion.
analysis.point2: The essay argues that formal schooling sometimes prevents true, self-directed learning.

For example, students learn to read books and write essays in daily life for many people in many places. As a result, they can share their ideas with others in daily life for many people. School also gives students important life skills. This is because learning in a group helps people talk to others in daily life for many people in many places. This supports the view that school helps people grow.

In conclusion, I strongly disagree with the view that school education interferes with learning. School helps students think better, and it also gives students important life skills.

analysis.point2: School provides important life skills, such as working in groups and talking to others.

title: #2 Healthy Diet
prompt: A healthy diet is more effective for keeping fit than exercise. What is your opinion?

variants.label: Version 1: AGREE
variants.essay:
People often talk about how to keep their body fit. In my opinion, I strongly agree with the view that a healthy diet is more effective for keeping fit than exercise. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

A healthy diet gives the body the right fuel it needs to stay strong. In other words, good food gives us the power to do daily tasks in daily life. For example, eating many fruits and vegetables gives us many vitamins. As a result, our body works well and feels good. This shows that good food is very important for a strong body.

Good food helps the body build muscle and keep bones strong. This is because the right food gives us the building blocks we need in daily life. For example, drinking milk and eating cheese gives us calcium for our bones. As a result, we can move better and feel more active. This supports the view that good food helps us stay fit.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that a healthy diet is more effective for keeping fit than exercise. Good food gives the body the right fuel, and good food helps the body build muscle and keep bones strong.

analysis.point1: A healthy diet provides the necessary fuel and nutrients for the body to function well and maintain strength.
analysis.point2: Proper nutrition supplies the building blocks needed to build strong muscles and keep bones healthy.

variants.label: Version 2: DISAGREE
variants.essay:
Keeping fit needs more than just good food; it also needs movement. In my opinion, I strongly disagree with the view that a healthy diet is more effective for keeping fit than exercise. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

Regular physical activity is very important for keeping the body fit. In other words, moving our bodies helps our muscles and heart work better in daily life. For example, running or playing sports makes our heart move blood well. As a result, we have more energy to do daily tasks. This shows that exercise is key for a strong body.

Diet alone cannot make a person fit enough. This is because the body needs movement to use the energy from the food we eat. For example, if we only eat good food and sit all day, our muscles become weak. As a result, our body does not use the food's energy properly. This supports the view that exercise is needed for fitness.

In conclusion, I strongly disagree with the view that a healthy diet is more effective for keeping fit than exercise. Both regular activity and good food are needed to keep the body fit and support a strong body.

analysis.point1: The essay argues that exercise is equally, if not more, important than diet for fitness.
analysis.point2: The essay uses concrete examples (running, playing sports) and clear effects (more energy, weak muscles) to support the argument.

title: #4 Advertising
prompt: Advertisements make people purchase things they don’t need or cannot afford, but they also convey information to increase people's life quality. What is your opinion?

variants.label: Version 1: NEGATIVE VIEW
variants.essay:
People have different ideas about advertisements and what they do for us. In my opinion, I strongly agree with the view that advertisements make people buy things they do not need or cannot afford. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

On the one hand, advertisements make people buy things they do not need or cannot afford. In other words, they make people want things they do not really need in daily life. For example, ads show people fancy phones that cost much money. As a result, people feel they must buy this phone to look good. This shows that ads can make people spend money they do not have.

On the other hand, advertisements also give people useful information. This is because ads can tell people about new services or better products in daily life. For example, ads might show a new type of healthy food. As a result, people learn about better ways to eat and live. This supports the view that ads can help people improve their life.

In conclusion, I strongly agree with the view that advertisements make people buy things they do not need or cannot afford. This is clear from hand and other.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that shoppers should avoid buying items with too much packaging. Both buyer choice and company methods are important for reducing waste and making better products.

In my opinion, I strongly agree with the view that the information revolution has more positive consequences than negative ones. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

On the one hand, the information revolution has significantly enhanced global connectivity and access to knowledge. In other words, the internet and digital platforms have democratized information sharing, making educational resources universally available. For instance, students in remote areas can now access prestigious university lectures through online courses. As a result, geographical limitations are minimized, allowing for unprecedented levels of self-directed learning. Hence, it becomes evident that this technological shift empowers individuals globally.

On the other hand, the information revolution presents certain drawbacks, such as the proliferation of misinformation. This is primarily due to the fact that the speed of content creation often outpaces the ability of fact-checkers to verify sources. This can be exemplified by the fact that fake news campaigns spread virally across social media platforms. The outcome is that public discourse can become polarized, undermining trust in established institutions. This clearly aligns with the view that managing the spread of false information is a significant challenge.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that the positive aspects of the information revolution outweigh the negative ones. While the challenge of misinformation exists, the unparalleled enhancement of global connectivity and access to knowledge solidifies this perspective.

analysis.point2: The main drawback is the rapid spread of misinformation, which poses a risk to public trust and stable discourse.

As a result, the overall quality of decision-making within government departments could suffer significantly. This is primarily due to the fact that talented people value autonomy and recognition based on their achievements. This can be exemplified by the fact that top-tier professionals prefer environments where their skills are the primary determinant of promotion. The outcome is that the workforce may become less innovative and more focused on navigating political requirements rather than solving complex problems. In conclusion, I strongly agree that placing advertisements in schools is a great resource for additional funding. Ads help schools buy needed items, and while ads might distract students, the financial help is more important.

Education helps people find good jobs. In other words, learning skills helps people get work in daily life for many people. For example, a student learns how to use a computer at school in daily life for many people. As a result, this person can get a job in an office in daily life. This shows that education helps people find good jobs.

Education helps people be good members of society. This is because learning about rules helps people live well together in daily life for many people. For example, people learn about helping others in their community in daily life for many people. As a result, they become responsible citizens who care for others in daily life. This supports the view that education helps people be good members of society.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that education helps people find good jobs and helps people be good members of society. These two areas show the true purpose of learning.

In conclusion, I strongly disagree with the view that the purpose of education is for individuals to fulfill their life. Education must prepare people for their jobs and also help people be good members of society.

variants.essay:
Many people spend too much time working and not enough time with their families or friends. In my opinion, I strongly agree with the view that people devoting too much time to their job is a widespread problem. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

The major reason is that people feel pressure to work long hours. In other words, people think they must always be busy to succeed in life. For example, many office workers stay late every day to finish big projects. As a result, their health gets bad, and they feel very tired. This shows that work pressure causes people to neglect their personal life.

One effective solution is for companies to change working hours. This is because shorter work days give people more time for other things. For example, a company could let staff leave at four o'clock instead of six o'clock. As a result, people can spend time on hobbies or with their family. This supports the view that better work hours help people balance their lives.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that devoting too much time to work is a problem. We must reduce work pressure and change working hours to help people live better lives.

For example, solar panels catch sunlight to make electricity for homes in daily life. As a result, we can reduce our use of dirty fuels and help the planet. This supports the view that using clean energy is very important.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that climate change is the most pressing global problem. We must address the major reason of human activities and adopt clean energy sources to help the planet.

People today throw away many things and make a lot of rubbish in the world. In my opinion, I strongly agree with the view that we have entered a throw-away society and must address it. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

The major reason is that people use things only once and throw them away. In other words, we buy items and use them for a short time in daily life. For example, plastic bottles are used for drinks and then thrown in the trash in daily life. As a result, the amount of waste grows very fast in daily life. This shows that we need to change how we use things.

One effective solution is to improve recycling systems in our towns. This is because recycling helps us use old materials again in daily life. For example, glass bottles can be cleaned and made into new items in daily life. As a result, less rubbish goes into the ground in daily life. This supports the view that better recycling is important.

In conclusion, I strongly agree with the view that we have entered a throw-away society and must address it. This is because people use items only once, and improving recycling systems helps us reuse old materials.

The decision for students to undertake part-time employment presents various considerations regarding their academic and personal growth. In my opinion, I strongly positive with positive. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

As a result, they develop a deeper understanding of workplace dynamics and professional etiquette. Hence, it becomes evident that part-time jobs significantly enhance a student's professional skill set.

Another benefit is the development of crucial time management abilities. This is primarily due to the fact that students must coordinate work schedules with their academic commitments. This can be exemplified by the fact that a student juggling classes and shifts learns to prioritize tasks effectively. The outcome is that they become adept at balancing multiple responsibilities, improving overall organizational skills. This clearly aligns with the view that part-time employment fosters superior self-discipline.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that part-time jobs are beneficial for students. These jobs enhance professional skill set through practical work experience and improve time management abilities by requiring students to balance multiple responsibilities.

variants.essay:
The decision for students to engage in part-time employment presents a complex issue regarding their academic pursuits. In my opinion, I strongly negative with negative. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

One major disadvantage is the potential disruption to academic commitments. In other words, balancing paid employment with rigorous coursework demands significant time and mental energy. For instance, a student working long hours may find insufficient time to dedicate to studying complex subjects. As a result, their grades might suffer, hindering their overall educational progress. Hence, it becomes evident that work can negatively impact academic performance.

Another significant drawback concerns the depletion of time needed for personal growth. This is primarily due to the fact that job responsibilities often consume hours that could be allocated to hobbies or rest. This can be exemplified by the fact that excessive work schedules limit opportunities for physical activity and social interaction. The outcome is that students may experience burnout and neglect crucial aspects of their well-being. This clearly aligns with the view that employment can compromise personal development.

In conclusion, I strongly disagree with the notion that part-time jobs are always beneficial. The potential negative impact on academic commitments and the depletion of time needed for personal growth suggest that students must proceed with caution.

On the one hand, libraries are becoming less important because digital books are easy to use. In other words, many students can find books on the internet quickly. For example, a university student can download a whole book onto a tablet. As a result, physical libraries need fewer people to run them. This shows that digital sources are better for learning today.

On the other hand, some people think libraries are still very important for students. This is because physical libraries offer a quiet place to study and read. For example, a student can go to the library and study without noise. As a result, they can focus on their school work better. This supports the view that libraries still have a strong place in education.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that libraries are becoming less important and universities should only procure digital media. Digital books are easy to use, and the need for a quiet place to study is less important than digital access.

The outcome is that the public becomes accustomed to extreme and over-the-top portrayals of human conflict. variants.label: Version 2: DISAGREE
variants.essay:
The discussion surrounding the promotion of violence through mass media is a frequently debated topic. In my opinion, I strongly disagree with disagree. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

Media content does not inherently promote aggression or violence. In other words, the consumption of such material is often a form of entertainment or social commentary. For instance, many historical dramas depict battles for narrative purposes, without encouraging real-world conflict. As a result, viewers tend to engage with the narrative elements rather than adopting the depicted actions. Hence, it becomes evident that the media functions more as a mirror reflecting society than a source of incitement.

Media consumption is primarily driven by the desire for information and escapism, not by a predisposition toward violence. This is primarily due to the fact that audiences seek diverse perspectives and engaging stories. This can be exemplified by the fact that documentaries explore complex social issues, such as poverty, without sensationalizing conflict. The outcome is that critical thinking skills are stimulated, allowing people to analyze difficult topics responsibly. This clearly aligns with the view that media serves an educational purpose, promoting understanding.

In conclusion, I strongly disagree with the notion that media promotes violence. The evidence suggests that media functions as a mirror reflecting society, and its consumption stimulates critical thinking, thereby serving an educational purpose.

This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

Choosing subjects that we are interested in is very important for students. In other words, learning subjects we enjoy makes school time better. For example, a student who likes art can spend hours drawing pictures. As a result, this activity helps them focus and feel happy at school. This shows that interest makes learning easier and more fun.

Another reason is that interest helps students learn better. This is because when we care about a subject, we try harder to understand it. For example, a student who likes history will read many books about old times. As a result, they will get good grades in history tests. This supports the view that interest helps students achieve good grades.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that students should choose subjects they are interested in. Focusing on subjects that we like helps students enjoy school, and this interest also helps them achieve good grades.

Credit cards are a common way for people to pay for things. In my opinion, I strongly positive with the view that a cashless society has more benefits than drawbacks. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

On the one hand, using credit cards makes shopping very easy. In other words, people do not need to carry much cash when they go out. For example, a person can buy food or clothes just by using a card. As a result, they save time and do not worry about losing money. This shows that credit cards make daily life simpler for many people.

On the other hand, there is a risk of debt when using credit cards. This is because people might spend more money than they actually have. For example, someone might buy many things they do not need right now. As a result, they can get into financial trouble and owe money. This supports the view that credit cards can cause money problems.

In conclusion, I strongly positive with the view that a cashless society has more benefits than drawbacks. This is because using cards makes daily life simpler, while it also highlights the risk of people spending more money than they have.

Air travel is a major part of modern life, and people often discuss its positive and negative effects. In my opinion, I strongly positive with the view that air travel has more positive impacts on modern life. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

On the one hand, air travel greatly helps people connect with others across long distances. In other words, it makes global movement much faster and easier for many people. For instance, a person can travel from one continent to another in just a few hours. As a result, businesses can operate globally, and families can visit relatives quickly. Hence, it becomes evident that air travel is vital for global connection and economic growth.

On the other hand, air travel has some negative impacts, such as pollution and carbon emissions. This is primarily due to the fact that planes burn fuel, which releases harmful gases into the air. This can be exemplified by the fact that large numbers of planes contribute to air pollution in major cities. The outcome is that the environment faces extra stress, and air quality can drop. This clearly aligns with the view that air travel presents environmental problems.

In conclusion, I strongly positive with the view that air travel has more positive impacts on modern life. While air travel does present environmental problems, its role in global connection and economic growth remains extremely important.

On the one hand, paid leave helps people rest and relax. In other words, it gives workers time away from work without losing money in daily life. For example, an employee can take a week off to visit family. As a result, they feel much better and more rested when they return to work. This shows that paid leave helps people feel happy and ready to work.

On the other hand, paid leave can sometimes be a disadvantage. This is because it might make some people think they take too many days off. For example, a person might use all their days off for short trips. As a result, the company might feel that the worker is not working enough. This supports the view that it can cause some problems for the company.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that paid leave is good. Paid leave helps people feel happy and ready to work, but it can also cause some problems for the company.

The major reason is that digitalization makes it easy for bad news to spread quickly. In other words, people do not check facts before they share information in daily life. For example, fake stories about health can spread on social media platforms in daily life. As a result, many people believe untrue things about their lives. This shows that the speed of digital life causes poor journalism.

One effective solution is that news organizations must teach people how to check sources. This is because readers need skills to tell good news from bad news in daily life. For example, schools can teach students to look at who wrote an article. As a result, people will become more careful when they read online content. This supports the view that education helps fix the problem.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that lazy journalism needs fixing. We must remember that digitalization causes problems, and teaching people to check sources is a good way to help.

The decline in journalistic quality, often termed lazy journalism, represents a significant challenge to informed public discourse. In my opinion, I strongly agree with the view that lazy journalism is caused by digitalization and must be addressed. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

The major reason is the pervasive influence of digital platforms on news consumption. In other words, the shift towards rapid, bite-sized content has diminished the incentive for deep investigative reporting. For instance, online news feeds prioritize sensational headlines over nuanced analysis, encouraging superficial coverage. As a result, journalists may feel compelled to publish quick, easily digestible articles rather than thorough, complex investigations. Hence, it becomes evident that the digital environment inherently promotes superficiality in media output.

One effective solution is the implementation of rigorous journalistic standards by educational institutions. This is primarily due to the fact that professional training must emphasize ethical responsibility and comprehensive research methods. This can be exemplified by the fact that universities could mandate advanced coursework focusing on fact-checking and source verification. The outcome is that future journalists would possess the necessary skills to resist the temptation of superficial reporting. This clearly aligns with the view that professional education is crucial for maintaining journalistic integrity.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that lazy journalism is a serious issue. Addressing this requires recognizing the digital platforms' influence and promoting rigorous journalistic standards to restore quality reporting.

Academic learning requires a dedicated and quiet environment to help students focus on their studies. In other words, the mental effort needed for learning is very different from the tasks done at a job. For instance, a student trying to read a complex book while working a retail shift will find it hard to concentrate. As a result, the student might perform poorly in both their classes and their job. Hence, it becomes evident that these two activities pull the student's attention in different directions.

A student's schedule needs time to dedicate to both schoolwork and work commitments. This is primarily due to the fact that managing two full routines takes up most of a person's waking hours. This can be exemplified by the fact that a student working forty hours a week will have little time left for homework or revision. The outcome is that the student must cut back on sleep or social time to keep up with both roles. This clearly aligns with the view that these two roles are difficult to manage at the same time.

In conclusion, I strongly agree with the view that it is impossible to combine study with employment because one distracts the other. This is because the contrasting demands of academic learning and professional tasks make concentration difficult, and managing two full routines severely limits the time available for both commitments.

Air pollution is a big problem for people and the planet. In my opinion, I strongly agree with the view that increasing fuel prices is the only way to reduce air pollution. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

Raising fuel prices helps people use cars less. In other words, higher costs make people think about their travel habits in daily life. For example, people might choose to walk or take the bus instead of driving a car. As a result, fewer cars will use the roads, which cleans the air. This shows that price changes can change people's actions.

Making fuel more expensive helps governments plan better transport systems. This is because people will need better public transport options if cars are costly in daily life. For example, cities can build more bus lanes and train lines for everyone. As a result, the public transport system gets better and more people use it. This supports the view that price changes help improve city services.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that increasing fuel prices is the only way to reduce air pollution. Raising fuel prices helps people change their travel habits, and this also helps governments improve public transport systems.

The debate concerning job prospects often involves weighing the importance of financial compensation against the quality of the working environment. In my opinion, I strongly disagree with the view that work conditions are more important when looking for a job. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

A primary consideration when seeking employment is the level of remuneration offered by an employer. In other words, a substantial salary provides the financial security necessary for maintaining a comfortable lifestyle. For instance, a graduate with specialized skills might receive a high starting salary in a major metropolitan area. As a result, this income allows them to afford better housing and educational opportunities for their family. Hence, it becomes evident that financial stability is a crucial foundation for any career.

Another compelling factor in career decisions is the overall workplace environment. This is primarily due to the fact that a positive atmosphere significantly contributes to employee morale and productivity. This can be exemplified by the fact that companies promoting work-life balance often report lower rates of burnout among staff. The outcome is that employees feel valued and are more inclined to commit to the organization long-term. This clearly aligns with the view that job fulfillment is paramount.

In conclusion, I strongly disagree with the view that work conditions are more important when looking for a job. This is because financial stability provides the necessary foundation for a comfortable life, while a positive workplace environment significantly enhances employee morale and commitment.

title: #112 Differential Education
prompt: Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of differential education, i.e., splitting students into different classes according to their academic performance.

variants.label: Version 1: ADVANTAGES
variants.essay:
Differential education means putting students into different classes based on how well they learn. In my opinion, I strongly positive with positive. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

One clear advantage is that students can learn at a good speed that suits them. In other words, students who learn fast can move quickly through the material in daily life in daily life. For example, students who understand math well can join a group that works on hard problems. As a result, these students feel challenged and keep learning new things. This shows that fast learners stay interested in school.

Another reason is that small groups help students who need more time to understand things. This is because students who learn slow need more support and attention in daily life. For example, students who have trouble with reading can join a small class with a teacher. As a result, the teacher can give them extra help and repeat the lesson. This supports the view that slow learners feel more confident in their studies.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that differential education is helpful. It helps fast learners stay interested and also supports slow learners who need more time.

variants.essay:
Differential education involves separating students into different classes based on their academic performance. In my opinion, I strongly positive with positive. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

One clear advantage is that students can receive instruction that matches their current academic ability. In other words, students who learn fast can move quickly through material, while those who learn slow get extra help. For instance, a class for advanced students might study complex physics, and another might focus on basic mechanics. As a result, students feel more comfortable and more motivated in their own learning group. Hence, it becomes evident that this approach helps close the learning gap.

Another reason is that small groups allow teachers to give more personal attention to each student. This is primarily due to the fact that teachers can see exactly where a student is struggling with a concept. This can be exemplified by the fact that a teacher can spend extra time with a small group needing help with writing essays. The outcome is that students gain confidence and improve their overall understanding of concepts. This clearly aligns with the view that focused teaching improves student progress.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that differential education is beneficial. This method helps students by matching their academic ability and also improves student progress through focused teaching.

Differential education involves separating students into different classes based on their academic performance. In my opinion, I strongly negative with negative. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

One major disadvantage is that it can create a feeling of separation among students. In other words, students who are grouped together may feel judged by their academic ability. For instance, a student who struggles might feel embarrassed when placed in a lower-level class. As a result, this feeling can lower their self-confidence and motivation to learn. Hence, it becomes evident that this approach harms the student's emotional well-being.

Another issue is that it might limit the overall learning experience for students. This is primarily due to the fact that the curriculum might become too narrow for some groups. This can be exemplified by the fact that advanced students might get bored with the limited material. The outcome is that these students miss out on opportunities to challenge themselves with broader topics. This clearly aligns with the view that a wider educational scope is needed.

In conclusion, I strongly disagree with differential education. This is because the separation of students into different classes harms emotional well-being, and it also limits the overall learning experience.

variants.essay:
Differential education involves dividing students into separate classes based on their academic performance and learning pace. In my opinion, I strongly positive with positive. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

One clear advantage of differential education is that it allows students to learn at an optimal pace. In other words, students who grasp concepts quickly can advance without waiting for their peers. For instance, a gifted mathematics class might cover advanced algebra while others review basic arithmetic. As a result, the advanced students remain engaged and challenged, preventing boredom. Hence, it becomes evident that this approach maximizes the potential of high-achieving learners.

Another benefit is that it provides targeted support for students who require extra academic attention. This is primarily due to the fact that small groups allow instructors to focus on specific knowledge gaps. This can be exemplified by the fact that a remedial reading group can dedicate time to phonics skills. The outcome is that struggling students receive intensive, personalized instruction they would not get in a large class. This clearly aligns with the view that academic disadvantage can be mitigated effectively.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that differential education is beneficial. By allowing students to learn at an optimal pace and providing targeted support for academic disadvantage, it significantly improves educational outcomes.

title: #114 Negative Impact
prompt: Poor lifestyles have a negative impact on people's health. List some unhealthy lifestyles and discuss what government services could help?

variants.label: Version 1: UNHEALTHY LIFESTYLES & SOLUTIONS
variants.essay:
Poor ways of living can make people sick and affect their health. In my opinion, I strongly agree with the view that poor lifestyles negatively impact health and government must help. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

The main cause is poor eating habits and lack of exercise. In other words, people often eat too much bad food and do not move enough in daily life. For example, many people prefer sweet drinks and chips instead of fresh fruit in daily life. As a result, they might get overweight and have bad health problems. This shows that poor diet and little activity are major problems.

One effective solution is that the government must offer better health services. This is because these services can teach people how to eat well and stay active in daily life. For example, the government can build more parks and offer free fitness classes in daily life. As a result, people will feel more motivated to walk and exercise outside. This supports the view that government help is very important.

In conclusion, I strongly agree with the view that poor lifestyles negatively impact health and government must help. This is because poor diet and lack of activity cause health issues, and government help can provide better services and facilities.

analysis.point1: The main cause of poor health is poor eating habits and lack of exercise, as people often consume bad food and do not move enough in daily life.
analysis.point2: The government can offer better health services, such as building parks and offering free fitness classes, to encourage people to stay active.

The major reason is that poor eating habits and lack of physical activity are common problems. In other words, many people do not eat enough healthy food, and they do not exercise enough. For instance, a diet high in sugar and processed food leads to weight gain. As a result, people face a higher risk of getting chronic illnesses like diabetes. One effective solution is for the government to run public health initiatives. This is primarily due to the fact that these programs can teach people how to live better. This can be exemplified by the fact that local councils can offer free classes on healthy cooking. The outcome is that people learn good habits and change their daily routines. This clearly aligns with the view that government support is needed for better health.

In conclusion, I strongly agree with the view that poor lifestyles negatively impact health and government must help. This is because poor eating habits and lack of physical activity pose significant health risks, and government initiatives can effectively educate people on adopting healthier routines.

variants.essay:
The question of whether children should participate in extra classes or engage in after-school play is a subject of considerable debate. In my opinion, I strongly agree with agree. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

Engaging in structured academic classes provides children with specialized knowledge that supports their intellectual growth. In other words, these classes allow students to deepen their understanding of specific subjects beyond the core curriculum. For instance, attending an advanced science workshop can expose a child to complex concepts not covered in regular school lessons. As a result, students develop a more robust academic skillset, which is beneficial for future studies. Hence, it becomes evident that structured learning significantly enhances a child's academic performance.

Furthermore, dedicating time to play outside of structured learning is crucial for developing essential social and emotional skills. This is primarily due to the fact that unstructured play requires children to interact and negotiate roles with their peers. This can be exemplified by the fact that playing team sports teaches cooperation and conflict resolution in a natural setting. The outcome is that children build stronger interpersonal relationships and learn valuable self-regulation techniques. This clearly aligns with the view that play is fundamental for emotional development.

In conclusion, I strongly agree with agree. This is clear from engaging and furthermore.

variants.essay:
The debate surrounding whether children should prioritize structured extra classes or unstructured after-school play is quite common. In my opinion, I strongly disagree with disagree. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

Focusing solely on academic classes can create undue pressure on young students. In other words, an overemphasis on structured learning diminishes the child's natural inclination for exploration. For instance, a child might be forced to attend advanced math tutoring, neglecting their interest in nature. As a result, this intense academic focus can lead to burnout and anxiety among the student body. Hence, it becomes evident that a balanced approach is far more beneficial for their overall well-being.

Prioritizing structured learning over free play can negatively impact a child's emotional development. This is primarily due to the fact that unstructured time is crucial for developing social skills. This can be exemplified by the fact that playing freely with peers allows children to negotiate rules and resolve conflicts naturally. The outcome is that they gain essential emotional intelligence and learn cooperation without direct instruction. This clearly aligns with the view that unstructured play is vital for a child's complete growth.

In conclusion, I strongly disagree with disagree. This is clear from focusing and prioritizing.

Many countries spend large amounts of money on restoring old buildings instead of building new houses. In my opinion, I strongly positive with the advantages outweigh the disadvantages. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

On the one hand, restoring old buildings helps keep safe the city's history and culture. In other words, these old structures hold important memories of past times. For instance, a restored old market can show the community's traditional way of life. As a result, people feel a stronger connection to their roots and local identity. Hence, it becomes evident that preservation supports community identity and history.

On the other hand, focusing on old buildings has a clear disadvantage for modern living. This is primarily due to the fact that old structures often need expensive repairs and updates. This can be exemplified by the fact that old plumbing and wiring systems are difficult to update for modern use. The outcome is that the cost of maintenance can take away money that could build new, practical homes. This clearly aligns with the view that development priorities should focus on modern housing needs.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that while preserving old buildings is important, the need for modern housing is also key. Both supporting community identity through old buildings and addressing the disadvantage of modern housing are necessary for a balanced city.

This clearly aligns with the view that biology is crucial for improving human health and understanding life.

title: #181 Two Roles of TV
prompt: Television has two roles: to inform and to entertain people. Explain which of these roles you see as more important. To what extent do you think that TV today performs each of these roles in an effective way? Support your point of view with details from your own experiences, observations or reading.

variants.label: Version 1: AGREE
variants.essay:
Television has two main jobs: it can teach us things, or it can make us feel happy. In my opinion, I strongly agree with agree. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

The role of TV to teach us things is very important. In other words, TV can help people learn about the world around them in daily life in daily life in daily life. For example, news programs show us about different countries and events in daily life. As a result, people know more facts and understand big issues. This shows that the educational role is very useful for our lives.

The role of TV to make us happy is also very important. This is because watching TV can give people a good time and make them feel relaxed in daily life in daily life. For example, family watching a comedy show together is fun in daily life in daily life. As a result, people spend good time with their family and feel happy. This supports the view that entertainment is good for our minds.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that both roles are important. TV helps us learn things, and it also gives us happy time.

The assertion that rapid urbanization is the sole effective remedy for unemployment is a highly debatable claim. In my opinion, I strongly disagree with disagree. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

A primary concern is that rapid urbanization often fails to generate sufficient employment opportunities for the influx of people. In other words, the pace of population movement frequently outstrips the capacity of local industries to absorb new labor. For instance, a sudden influx of migrants into a major city can overwhelm existing service sectors, such as construction and retail. As a result, many individuals find themselves relegated to precarious, low-wage jobs, leading to increased poverty. Hence, it becomes evident that simply moving people to a city does not guarantee economic stability or job creation.

Another critical issue is that economic development requires more than just population concentration; it needs robust infrastructure and planning. This is primarily due to the fact that uncontrolled urban expansion strains public resources, including housing and sanitation systems. This can be exemplified by the fact that many developing conurbations lack adequate public transportation, forcing reliance on costly private vehicles. The outcome is that the quality of life diminishes for all residents, regardless of their employment status. This clearly aligns with the view that sustainable development must guide any attempt to improve livelihoods.

In conclusion, I strongly disagree with disagree. This is clear from primary and another.

On the one hand, One clear advantage is that living in these groups gives old people good company. In other words, they meet many friends who are at a similar life stage. For example, they can join group activities like singing or playing games. As a result, they feel less lonely and more happy every day. This shows that this living choice helps people feel connected to their peers.

On the other hand, Another reason is that this living choice can cause problems for family ties. This is because people might spend all their time with new friends and forget their children. For example, they might lose contact with their own family members. As a result, family bonds can become weak, and people may feel apart from their kin. This supports the view that family relationships can suffer.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that the advantages outweigh the disadvantages. Living in groups gives good company, but this choice can also cause family relationships to suffer.

variants.essay:
As societies advance and people's lifestyles become more settled, the relationship between humans and domestic pets is evolving significantly. In my opinion, I strongly agree with agreeing with the statement. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

The deep emotional connection formed with pets is a significant factor in this trend. In other words, pets provide unconditional affection and emotional support to their owners. For instance, elderly individuals often find great comfort in the routine care of a cat or dog. As a result, the presence of a pet can mitigate feelings of loneliness and isolation. Hence, it becomes evident that pets are viewed as integral members of the family unit.

Furthermore, the concept of pet ownership reflects a growing sense of responsibility and attachment. This is primarily due to the fact that modern life allows for greater time and resources dedicated to animal welfare. This can be exemplified by the fact that many people invest in specialized pet care services and high-quality food. The outcome is that pet owners feel a profound sense of duty, treating their animals with utmost care. This clearly aligns with the view that pets are cherished companions deserving of familial consideration.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that pets are increasingly regarded as family members. The profound emotional connection and the sense of responsibility associated with pet ownership solidify this view.

analysis.point1: The emotional bond between humans and pets is growing stronger, making them feel like family.
analysis.point2: The modern lifestyle allows people to take on greater responsibility for their pets, reinforcing their status as family.

variants.label: Version 2: DISAGREE
variants.essay:
The increasing tendency for people to view domestic pets as integral family members is a widely discussed modern phenomenon. In my opinion, I strongly disagree with disagree. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

This attachment blurs the traditional boundaries between human and animal companionship. In other words, pet ownership often involves emotional investment comparable to that of a human relative. For instance, many individuals spend considerable funds on specialized pet care and gourmet food. As a result, the pet becomes viewed not merely as an animal, but as a cherished member of the household. Hence, it becomes evident that this emotional attachment can lead to undue financial and emotional burdens on the owners.

Furthermore, this perception can diminish the necessary sense of personal responsibility. This is primarily due to the fact that people may underestimate the complex needs of an animal. This can be exemplified by the fact that some owners neglect necessary veterinary check-ups or proper exercise routines. The outcome is that the animal's welfare suffers, potentially leading to behavioral issues or health complications. This clearly aligns with the view that emotional attachment must be balanced with practical animal welfare considerations.

In conclusion, I strongly disagree with disagree. This is clear from attachment and furthermore.

title: #214 Children Advertisement
prompt: Nowadays, there are many television advertisements aimed at children. Should television advertisements be controlled or not?

variants.label: Version 1: OPTION A
variants.essay:
Many television advertisements are made for children today. In my opinion, I strongly agree with agree. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

These ads can show children things they want to buy. In other words, they make kids feel they need certain toys or items in daily life. For example, a cartoon might show a character using a specific brand of snack. As a result, the child wants that snack and asks their parents for it. This shows that ads can change what children want to play with.

Controlling these ads helps keep children safe from bad ideas. This is because some ads show things that are not good for kids to see in daily life. For example, an ad might show too much action or scary things. As a result, children might feel worried or scared when they watch TV. This supports the view that rules are needed for TV ads.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that TV ads for kids must be controlled. We must control the ads because they change what children want to play with, and we must control the ads because they show things that are not good for kids to see.

The notion that vegetarianism is inherently superior to omnivorous diets is a subject of considerable debate among the public. In my opinion, I strongly disagree with disagreeing with the statement. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

Omnivorous diets provide a comprehensive spectrum of nutrients essential for optimal human health. In other words, consuming a varied diet that includes animal products ensures the intake of vital nutrients often lacking in plant-based alternatives. For instance, red meat is a rich source of bioavailable iron and vitamin B12, which are crucial for blood formation and nerve function. As a result, individuals who restrict their diet may experience deficiencies that negatively impact their overall physical well-being. Hence, it becomes evident that a balanced diet incorporating all food groups is necessary for robust health.

Furthermore, the argument that vegetarianism is environmentally sound overlooks the complexity of modern agricultural practices. This is primarily due to the fact that sustainable farming methods can integrate livestock management with crop cultivation, optimizing land use. This can be exemplified by the fact that rotational grazing systems improve soil fertility and carbon sequestration on farms. The outcome is that these integrated systems reduce the need for chemical fertilizers and minimize habitat degradation. This clearly aligns with the view that responsible farming practices can support both animal welfare and ecological stability.

In conclusion, I strongly disagree with the notion that vegetarianism is universally superior; maintaining an omnivorous diet ensures vital nutrients, while responsible farming practices can support both animal welfare and ecological stability.

title: #246 Lifetime Employment
prompt: Businesses should employ people for life. What are the advantages and disadvantages of lifetime employment system?

variants.label: Version 1: ADVANTAGES
variants.essay:
Many people talk about keeping workers with one company for their whole working life. In my opinion, I strongly positive with the advantages outweigh the disadvantages. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

On the one hand, One clear advantage is that this system gives workers a strong feeling of job safety. In other words, workers know they will keep their job for a long time in daily life. For example, a person who works at a bank for many years feels safe. As a result, the worker can plan their life without worry. This shows that the worker feels happy and settled at the company.

On the other hand, Another reason is that this system has a negative point for the company. This is because workers might become too comfortable and stop learning new skills. For example, an old worker might refuse to use new computer programs. As a result, the company cannot grow or change its methods. This supports the view that the company needs new ideas and skills.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that the advantages are important. Job safety is good for workers, and the company also needs workers to learn new skills to keep growing.

analysis.point1: The first advantage is that the system provides workers with a strong feeling of job safety, allowing them to plan their lives without worry.
analysis.point2: A disadvantage is that workers might become too comfortable and stop learning new skills, which prevents the company from growing or changing its methods.

variants.label: Version 2: DISADVANTAGES
variants.essay:
Lifetime employment means a person works for one company for many years. In my opinion, I strongly negative with the disadvantages outweigh the advantages. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

On the one hand, this type of work gives people job security. In other words, workers know they have a job for a long time in daily life. For example, a person might work at a bank for twenty years in daily life. As a result, the worker feels safe and does not worry about losing work. This shows that job security helps people plan their lives.

On the other hand, this system has a major disadvantage for workers. This is because it can stop people from finding new skills in daily life. For example, if a company does not change, the worker does not learn new things in daily life. As a result, the worker might feel stuck in their job and cannot move up. This supports the view that lack of new skills is a problem.

In conclusion, I strongly negative with the disadvantages outweigh the advantages. This is because job security helps people plan their lives, but it also stops workers from finding new skills.

variants.label: Version 2: OPTION B
variants.essay:
The process of making significant life choices is often debated, particularly whether such decisions should be made in isolation. In my opinion, I strongly disagree with disagree. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

Making major decisions alone can lead to significant blind spots regarding potential consequences. In other words, an individual's perspective is inherently limited, restricting their view of the full scope of the issue. For instance, a person might overlook financial implications when choosing a career path without consulting experts. As a result, the individual may commit to a venture that is unsustainable or poorly suited to their overall goals. Hence, it becomes evident that relying solely on personal judgment introduces unnecessary risk.

Conversely, relying on group input can introduce a different set of complications. This is primarily due to the fact that group dynamics can sometimes lead to groupthink, where conformity overrides critical thought. This can be exemplified by the fact that a team might agree on a flawed plan simply to maintain harmony and avoid conflict. The outcome is that genuinely innovative or dissenting ideas are suppressed, resulting in a mediocre consensus. This clearly aligns with the view that group pressure can compromise objective decision-making.

In conclusion, I strongly disagree with disagree. This is clear from making and conversely.

This supports the view that slow life builds strong relationships.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that a slow-paced life is better. Taking time to enjoy activities and building strong relationships are two main benefits of a slow life.

variants.label: Version 2: DISADVANTAGES
variants.essay:
Tree-planting Day is a globally celebrated event intended to promote environmental awareness and reforestation efforts. In my opinion, I strongly negative with negative. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

One significant drawback of these organized events is the potential for superficial engagement with environmental issues. In other words, participation might become merely a photo opportunity rather than a commitment to long-term ecological stewardship. For instance, many participants view planting as a single, isolated action, neglecting the subsequent care required for the saplings. As a result, the survival rate of the newly planted trees often declines due to insufficient maintenance or proper species selection. Hence, it becomes evident that the immediate impact of the day is often overstated compared to sustained effort.

Another concern relates to the logistical challenges and the potential for resource misallocation. This is primarily due to the fact that organizing such large-scale events requires substantial financial and human capital. This can be exemplified by the fact that the procurement of appropriate tools, transportation, and expert labor can strain local community budgets. The outcome is that funds might be diverted from more critical, continuous environmental projects, such as pollution monitoring or habitat restoration. This clearly aligns with the view that the focus should be on systemic change rather than singular, annual activities.

In conclusion, I strongly disagree with the notion that Tree-planting Day is a complete solution. While the intention to promote environmental awareness is commendable, the superficial engagement and the resource misallocation issues diminish its overall effectiveness.

variants.label: Version 1: ADVANTAGES
variants.essay:
Many students sometimes take a break from school before starting college. In my opinion, I strongly positive with the advantages outweigh the disadvantages. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

On the one hand, taking a break year can help students learn about life. In other words, this time lets them try new things outside of school. For example, they can travel to a new city or help with a family business. As a result, they learn how to manage money and talk to different people. This shows that a break year helps students become more independent.

On the other hand, a gap year can also present a problem for students. This is because it might make it hard for students to remember what they learned in class. For example, they might spend time working in a shop instead of studying. As a result, their school knowledge might feel old or difficult to use. This supports the view that a break year can cause a knowledge gap.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that taking a break year is good. The chance to learn about life is a big plus, but the knowledge gap is a risk to think about.

Some people think that traditional cultures should change, but others think they should stay the same. In my opinion, I strongly agree with supporting the first viewpoint. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

On the one hand, traditional cultures keep important parts of a community alive. In other words, these cultures pass down old ways of life and customs in daily life. For example, many villages still celebrate old harvest festivals. As a result, people feel a strong connection to their history and roots. This shows that keeping traditions helps people feel connected to their past.

On the other hand, some people think that modern life makes cultures change too much. This is because new ideas and technology move fast. For example, young people now use phones for talking and learning. As a result, old ways of doing things might seem slow or difficult. This supports the view that change is hard to stop in the modern world.

title: #305 Lifelong Employment
prompt: Businesses should hire employees for their entire lives. Discuss the advantages or disadvantages of this.

variants.label: Version 1: ADVANTAGES
variants.essay:
Some people think that companies should keep workers for their whole working lives. In my opinion, I strongly positive with the advantages outweigh the disadvantages. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

On the one hand, Long-term working gives workers good job security. In other words, workers feel safe at their company for many years in daily life. For example, a person who works at one place for many years learns all the company's ways in daily life. As a result, the company saves money on training new people in daily life. This shows that long-term working helps the company stay strong.

On the other hand, Another reason is that long-term working can stop workers from changing. This is because workers might become too comfortable in their current roles in daily life. For example, an older worker might refuse to learn new computer skills in daily life. As a result, the company cannot grow or change its methods. This supports the view that this system stops progress.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that companies should keep workers for their whole working lives. Long-term working helps the company stay strong, and it is important for the company to continue progress.

The outcome is that the company's overall adaptability suffers, hindering its ability to compete in modern markets. The notion that individuals should participate in activities they do not find pleasurable is a common debate. In my opinion, I strongly disagree with disagree. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

Forcing people to engage in activities they dislike can be detrimental to their overall well-being. In other words, mandatory participation undermines the intrinsic motivation required for genuine engagement. For instance, compelling a student to take an elective they find boring reduces their enthusiasm for learning. As a result, the student may develop a negative association with the subject, diminishing their academic interest. Hence, it becomes evident that personal choice is crucial for maintaining mental health and sustained effort.

Furthermore, disregarding personal inclinations can severely impact self-esteem and emotional balance. This is primarily due to the fact that constant compulsion creates feelings of resentment and resistance. This can be exemplified by the fact that an employee forced into an undesirable role will experience chronic job dissatisfaction. The outcome is that this dissatisfaction can lead to burnout and decreased productivity across the workplace. This clearly aligns with the view that self-directed activities are essential for emotional stability and personal growth.

In conclusion, I strongly disagree with disagree. This is clear from forcing and furthermore.

title: #359 Lifetime Employment
prompt: Businesses should hire employees for their entire life. What is the disadvantage? What is your solution?

variants.label: Version 1: PROBLEMS & SOLUTIONS
variants.essay:
Some people think that businesses should keep workers for their whole lives. In my opinion, I strongly agree with identifying problems and proposing solutions. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

The major reason is that long-term employment can make workers less skilled. In other words, workers might stop learning new things after many years in daily life. For example, a person who works in the same job for thirty years might not learn about new computer programs today. As a result, the company cannot use the worker's skills for modern tasks. This shows that keeping people in one job for a long time is not good for the company.

One effective solution is that companies should offer training programs. This is because training helps workers learn new skills for their jobs in daily life. For example, a company can pay for a worker to take a course on digital marketing in daily life. As a result, the worker can use modern skills and help the company grow. This supports the view that giving workers training is a good idea.

In conclusion, I strongly agree with identifying problems and proposing solutions. This is because long-term jobs can make workers less skilled, and companies should offer training programs to help workers learn new skills.

analysis.point1: The main problem with keeping workers for their whole lives is that they might stop learning new skills, making them less useful to the company.
analysis.point2: A good solution is for companies to offer training programs, which helps workers learn new skills and keeps them useful.

Teaching financial management skills to children should be a core component of the educational curriculum. In my opinion, I strongly disagree with disagree. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

While financial literacy is undeniably valuable, formal schooling may not be the optimal environment for teaching these practical skills. In other words, the classroom setting often lacks the real-world context necessary for mastering money management. For instance, learning to budget with pocket money from a local shop provides far greater insight than theoretical lessons. As a result, students fail to grasp the immediate consequences of spending decisions in a simulated environment. Hence, it becomes evident that practical, experiential learning methods are superior for developing sound financial habits.

Furthermore, financial education should be acquired through family interaction and mentorship, not solely through academic institutions. This is primarily due to the fact that family units provide continuous, personalized guidance regarding household finances. This can be exemplified by the fact that observing parents manage a monthly budget teaches invaluable prioritization skills. The outcome is that children develop a natural understanding of income and expenses within a supportive domestic setting. This clearly aligns with the view that familial instruction is the most effective source of financial wisdom.

In conclusion, I strongly disagree with disagree. This is clear from while and furthermore.

The funding of art and culture is a subject of debate, concerning whether public or private entities should bear the primary financial responsibility. In my opinion, I strongly agree with agree. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

Government funding is crucial for maintaining cultural institutions and promoting artistic merit. In other words, state support ensures that cultural activities are accessible to all socioeconomic groups. For instance, public museums often receive subsidies that allow them to display historical artifacts regardless of commercial appeal. As a result, the preservation of local heritage is guaranteed, making these resources available for public enjoyment. Hence, it becomes evident that government involvement is essential for broad cultural preservation.

Private investment also plays a vital role in sustaining the creative economy and fostering community arts. This is primarily due to the fact that private sponsors introduce market dynamism and innovative funding streams. This can be exemplified by the fact that corporate philanthropy often supports niche art shows that might otherwise lack financial backing. The outcome is that the arts sector receives diversified capital, leading to greater artistic freedom. This clearly aligns with the view that private sector investment complements state efforts.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that both government and private investment are necessary. Government support is vital for cultural preservation, while private sector investment enhances the creative economy, ensuring a rich cultural landscape for everyone.

title: #387 Balance and Media
prompt: Are there practical solutions or guidelines for maintaining a healthy balance with social media?

variants.label: Version 1: PROBLEMS & SOLUTIONS
variants.essay:
Social media can make it hard to keep a good balance in life. In my opinion, I strongly agree with identifying problems and proposing solutions. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

The major reason is that people spend too much time online. In other words, using social media takes up many hours each day in daily life. For example, students might spend all their free time looking at pictures in daily life. As a result, they do not have time for hobbies or family time in daily life. This shows that too much time online hurts daily life.

One effective solution is to set clear time limits for social media use. This is because having rules helps people use the apps better in daily life. For example, a person can decide to only check the apps after dinner in daily life. As a result, they keep their focus on real-life activities during the day in daily life. This supports the view that setting limits helps people manage their time.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that identifying problems and proposing solutions is important. We must manage the time online and set clear time limits to achieve a good balance.

For instance, seeing friends' perfect vacations can make users feel bad about their own lives. As a result, this constant comparison can cause anxiety and stress. Hence, it becomes evident that identifying this problem is the first step toward improvement.

One effective solution is setting clear time limits for social media use. This is primarily due to the fact that limiting screen time helps people focus on real-life activities. This can be exemplified by the fact that setting a 'no phone' rule during meals improves family talks. The outcome is that people spend more quality time with family and friends. This clearly aligns with the view that practical solutions are necessary for better well-being.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that addressing the problem of comparison and implementing solutions like setting time limits are important for maintaining a healthy balance.

One effective solution is that schools can give students more support. This is because extra help makes it easier for students to feel confident in their studies. For example, a school could offer online study groups or extra one-on-one time with a teacher. As a result, students feel less alone and know who to ask for help. This supports the view that good support helps students learn better.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that identifying problems and proposing solutions is helpful. Managing study time is a key problem, and good support is an effective solution for students.

variants.essay:
The influence of social media platforms on the formation of public opinion is a subject of considerable debate. In my opinion, I strongly negative with negative. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

One major concern is the rapid dissemination of misinformation across these platforms. In other words, false or misleading content can spread with alarming speed, bypassing traditional journalistic checks. For instance, fabricated health claims circulated during a pandemic demonstrated this vulnerability. As a result, individuals may form deeply flawed understandings of critical global issues. Hence, it becomes evident that the integrity of public discourse is severely compromised.

Another significant issue involves the creation of echo chambers within online communities. This is primarily due to the fact that algorithms prioritize content that confirms existing beliefs, limiting exposure to diverse viewpoints. This can be exemplified by the fact that users are only shown posts aligning with their established political leanings. The outcome is that polarization increases, making constructive dialogue exceedingly difficult. This clearly aligns with the view that social media hinders genuine intellectual exchange.

In conclusion, I strongly disagree with the notion that social media is beneficial; its capacity for misinformation and its role in creating echo chambers fundamentally undermine public opinion.

A four-day week can help people work better. In other words, people have more time to rest and relax in daily life for many people. For example, workers can use the extra day to do chores or spend time with family in daily life. As a result, they feel more rested and have more energy for their jobs in daily life. This shows that a shorter week helps people work better.

A four-day week can help people balance their life better. This is because having more free time helps people manage their personal life in daily life. For example, students can attend classes or people can visit friends in another city in daily life. As a result, people feel happier and have more time for hobbies in daily life. This supports the view that a shorter week helps people balance life better.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that a four-day week is better. The shorter week helps people work better, and it also helps people balance life better.

Learning a second language helps people talk to more people. In other words, it opens up many chances to meet new friends in daily life for many people. For example, a person who learns Spanish can talk with people in Mexico in daily life for many people. As a result, they can understand local customs and talk about their lives in daily life. This shows that language skills help people connect with others.

Learning a second language helps people understand other cultures. This is because it gives them a new way to see the world in daily life for many people. For example, studying Japanese helps a person understand Japanese history in daily life for many people. As a result, they learn about different ways of life and traditions in daily life. This supports the view that language learning broadens one's view of the world.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that learning a second language is very important. It helps people connect with others and also helps people understand other cultures.

For example, many shops sell sugary drinks and chips near homes in daily life. As a result, people eat junk food often, and they do not eat good food in daily life. One effective solution is to plan meals and cook at home more often. This is because cooking at home gives people control over what they eat in daily life. For example, a family can plan a week of meals with fresh vegetables in daily life. As a result, they eat more balanced food and feel better each day. This supports the view that planning meals helps people eat well.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that identifying problems and proposing solutions is important. Easy access to bad food is a major issue, and planning meals can help people eat well.

The notion that virtual reality will fundamentally transform entertainment is overstated. The outcome is that the emotional depth and accessibility of these established formats remain unmatched by current VR simulations. This clearly aligns with the view that other forms of media will continue to dominate the market.

In conclusion, I strongly disagree with disagree. This is clear from notion and furthermore.

This clearly aligns with the view that moderation should remain with the users, not the platforms.

The outcome is that these platforms effectively become arbiters of truth, limiting diverse viewpoints. This clearly aligns with the view that individual autonomy in speech is paramount.

In conclusion, I strongly disagree with disagree. This is clear from regulating and furthermore.

Incorporating video games into education and skill development is a popular topic of discussion. In my opinion, I strongly negative with negative. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

One major disadvantage is that games might distract students from serious academic work. In other words, the fun nature of games can make it hard for students to focus on difficult subjects. For instance, a student might spend too much time playing a game instead of reading a textbook chapter. As a result, their study time decreases, and they might fall behind in their school work. Hence, it becomes evident that games can take away from necessary study time.

Another issue is that the content of games may not match the required curriculum content. This is primarily due to the fact that game developers focus on entertainment, not on educational goals. This can be exemplified by the fact that a history game might simplify complex events for fun. The outcome is that students learn incomplete or incorrect information, which is bad for their knowledge. This clearly aligns with the view that games lack proper educational structure.

In conclusion, I strongly disagree with the idea of using games in education. Games can distract students from academic work, and they may also lack proper educational structure.
